definition: The set of all possible outcomes of a trial, written $U$; $n(U)$ is the number of outcomes in it.
A set of outcomes from the sample space, such as "an odd number"; the event happens when the outcome of the trial is one of them.
The number of times an event happened divided by the number of trials: an experimental estimate of its probability, unlike the theoretical $\frac{n(A)}{n(U)}$, which needs equally likely outcomes.
An event $A$ and its complement $A'$ (not $A$), which holds every outcome not in $A$; exactly one of them happens on each trial, so $\mathrm{P}(A) + \mathrm{P}(A') = 1$.
The long-run average number of times an event $A$ happens in $n$ trials, $n \times \mathrm{P}(A)$; it need not be a whole number.
